summary: A Canary Capital issuer page currently exposes an XRPC holdings row dated 9 Nov 2026, future relative to the 7 Nov capture. That row reports 242,962,753.64 XRP and 22,920,000 shares. CryptoKeyhole and XRP Insights attribute essentially the exact same 242,962,754 XRP holdings quantity to 6 Nov. CryptoKeyhole also states its latest issuer file is dated 9 Nov. This is strong evidence of future-date/source-vintage contamination in the aggregators' 6 Nov XRPC observation. Reject the -752,048 XRP partial XRPC figure as a valid 6 Nov flow and quarantine the -663,043 XRP XRP Insights aggregate pending fund-level date reconciliation.

requirements: Set source_data_as_of_utc from the underlying issuer row's actual effective/as-of date, not the aggregator's displayed observation date.
If a page contains multiple dated rows, isolate the exact row whose effective date is no later than the forecast cutoff.
If a future-dated row is present and the requested historical row cannot be isolated, mark the observation provisional and model-ineligible.
Never backdate a later holdings snapshot to an earlier flow date.
Label holdings deltas separately from issuer-confirmed creations/redemptions.
Keep retrieval time, page update time, issuer row effective date, event time and first public availability separate.
point_in_time_ingestion_guard.current_feature_store_behavior: The existing point-in-time validator already rejects source_data_as_of_utc after cutoff. The remaining risk is parser/adapter mislabeling of a future issuer row as an earlier aggregator observation date; no normalized ETF-flow adapter is currently implemented.
